title: Prepare wavefunk-ui for first project integrations
description: Make wavefunk-ui ready to use as the common Askama + htmx UI base for new Wave Funk Rust projects. The crate must stay publishable, ship self-contained CSS/fonts/JS, support fast local iteration through gitignored consumer path overrides, and provide enough typed components, docs, and browser QA to unblock a separate first-consumer integration epic.

title: Stabilize the public component API contract
description: Define the public API rules for typed Askama components: naming, builder patterns, htmx attrs, HTML escaping and trusted slots, error handling, feature flags, and semver expectations. Acceptance: README and AGENTS document the contract; component constructors follow one consistent pattern; examples show safe attrs and safe inner HTML slots.
notes: Askama integration research: prefer exported Rust component types plus HtmlSafe over asking consumer crates to import template macro files from this crate. Askama macro/import/include paths are resolved at the deriving crate's compile time through that crate's template dirs, so dependency-crate macro files are awkward for crates.io consumers. Useful supported patterns: templates-in-templates with nested Template values; implement askama::filters::HtmlSafe for wavefunk component types so consumers can render {{ component }} without |safe; use call-block macros only inside this crate's own templates/gallery; expose public helper functions/newtypes for safe asset links and htmx attributes; use block/blocks for internal partials, not as the cross-crate API.
close_reason: Done: component API contract documented and backed by builders, htmx attr helpers, TrustedHtml slots, tests, and gallery examples.

title: Harden embedded asset distribution
description: Make the embedded asset API production-ready for self-contained binaries. Cover CSS/fonts/wavefunk.js/htmx/SSE, content types, cache policy, optional Axum router, framework-neutral lookup, license notes, and a stable default mount path. Acceptance: cargo package includes every asset; tests cover key assets and path rejection; docs show how consumers mount assets without runtime static directories.
close_reason: Done: embedded assets cover CSS/fonts/Wave Funk JS/htmx/SSE with constants, content types, cache policy, path normalization, package verification, and docs.

title: Port action and form primitives
description: Add typed Askama wrappers for the components most projects need immediately: icon button, button group, split button, input, textarea, select, input group, checkbox/radio row, switch, range, and form field variants. Acceptance: each wrapper renders Wave Funk markup, supports htmx attrs where relevant, has tests for escaping/classes, and appears in the gallery.
close_reason: Done: action and form wrappers added with tests for classes, escaping, htmx attrs, and gallery coverage.

title: Port layout, navigation, and data-display primitives
description: Add typed Askama wrappers for app shell variants, panel, card, table, definition list, stat, badge, avatar, breadcrumbs, tabs, segmented control, pagination, sidebar/topbar helpers, statusbar, empty state, and basic grid/split layout. Acceptance: wrappers cover the common app-page patterns needed by Sendword-style projects and render in the gallery.
close_reason: Done: layout, navigation, data-display, app-shell variant helpers, tests, and gallery coverage added.

title: Port feedback, overlay, and htmx interaction primitives
description: Add wrappers and JS conventions for modal, drawer, popover/menu, toast, echo/minibuffer, tooltip, skeleton, spinner, alert/callout variants, and htmx response helper functions. Acceptance: header-triggered toasts/echo work in browser QA; modal/popover/drawer behavior is documented; no consumer-specific JS leaks into the shared crate.

title: Validate Askama performance and local rebuild ergonomics
description: Apply Askama performance guidance to this crate and consumer usage. Acceptance: docs tell consumers to use render/render_into/write_into instead of to_string/format for templates; dev profile optimizes askama_derive; local path override rebuild times are checked with a template-heavy example; identify any types that should implement FastWritable.

title: Build a complete gallery and browser QA surface
description: Turn the current Axum example into the integration readiness gallery. It should render every public component, exercise embedded assets, htmx interactions, light/dark mode, dense/default density, and responsive app-shell behavior. Acceptance: agent-browser smoke checks cover page load, asset requests, toasts/echo, and representative interactions with no console errors.

title: Prove integration in one real Wave Funk consumer
description: Integrate wavefunk-ui into one existing Wave Funk Rust app using a gitignored .cargo/config.toml path override for local iteration while keeping the committed manifest on the crates.io dependency. Acceptance: the consumer mounts embedded assets, renders at least one shared layout and several shared components, builds as a self-contained binary, and verifies release/CI would resolve crates.io without the local override.

title: Finish crates.io and release readiness
description: Prepare the crate for the first published release after the core readiness work is complete. Acceptance: README examples are accurate, include list is complete, license/third-party notices are present, cargo package and cargo publish --dry-run pass, versioning/release notes are defined, and any CI/release workflow is in place.
